points.heading: This week in one picture
points.body:
Central idea: Spanish verb forms tell when an action happens.

Explore: Simple forms have one word; compound forms use haber plus a participle.

Practice: Explain the difference between «canté» and «he cantado» with your own example.

Common mistake: Do not only repeat names; use an example to show the meaning.

points.heading: One-word forms
points.body:
Central idea: Simple forms use one word.

Explore: Canto, cantaba, canté, cantaré, and cantaría show different times or possibilities.

Practice: Say the five forms and write a sentence for each.

Common mistake: Do not use cantaba for a closed yesterday event.

points.heading: Two-word forms
points.body:
Central idea: Compound forms use haber and a participle.

Explore: In «he cantado», the helper changes for the person but cantado stays the same.

Practice: Write three sentences using he cantado, había cantado, and habría cantado.

Common mistake: Do not change the participle to match the subject.

points.heading: How to choose
points.body:
Central idea: Choose the tense by asking what you want your story to show.

Explore: A closed action, a result that matters now, and a past habit need different forms.

Practice: Sort five sentences into those three ideas.

Common mistake: Do not ignore a time clue in the sentence.

points.heading: Finish
points.body:
Central idea: Clear grammar helps you tell a clear story.

Explore: First choose simple or compound; then choose the time that fits.

Practice: Write four sentences about your week using one simple and one compound form.

Common mistake: Do not memorize a list without using it.

lesson.summary: This lesson teaches review spanish indicative tenses. Understand the central idea first, then explore it, practice it, and check a common mistake.
